title: Symplectic Transport and Dissipative Learning
subtitle: A geometric basement for adaptive MMALS host networks
summary: Unitary quantum dynamics can be represented as a special orthogonal-symplectic flow. MMALS uses the broader insight more cautiously: symplectic geometry transports structured state, port-Hamiltonian dissipation stabilizes and consolidates it, Fisher--Rao geometry updates beliefs, and goal-conditioned control allocates resources.
claims: Unitary evolution embeds in the orthogonal-symplectic subgroup.
A larger transformation group is not by itself a complexity advantage.
Pure symplectic flow cannot provide forgetting or attractor-based consolidation.
Fisher--Rao and symplectic geometry play complementary roles.
MMALS action must be competence-aware, not coverage-only.
evidence_status: Theoretical synthesis grounded in prior MMALS evidence; dedicated symplectic MMALS experiments pending.
